statement: The FOMC raises the target range by 25 bp on 2026-10-28, to 4.00-4.25% (upper limit 4.25% on 2026-10-29).
basis: September's hike was unanimous and the statement said the Committee 'will deliver price stability' with 2026 PCE inflation projected at 3.7%; the September SEP median of 4.1% for end-2026 implies one more hike in two meetings; the 3-month bill sits 37 bp above the effective funds rate, which is roughly one hike at the next meeting plus part of another; no financial-stress reason to wait (HY spread 3.27%, VIX 16.7). Downside: a weak October labour report or a credit event.

statement: The 10-year Treasury yield on 2026-12-31 is between 4.60% and 5.30%.
basis: The 42 bp rise since July is real yield (+33 bp) and term premium (+14 bp), not inflation expectations (+4 bp); the 10-year expected short rate implied by the term-premium model (4.14%) already matches the SEP's 2026-27 medians, so the hiking path is priced; a market that has priced the path tends to range. Upside break above the 2026-10-05 high of 5.31% if the October statement signals a series; a fall below 4.60% needs a growth scare.

statement: The 2s10s slope (10-year minus 2-year) on 2026-12-31 is below 0.32 percentage points, i.e. the curve is flatter than on 2026-10-21.
basis: Hikes lift the 2-year more than the 10-year late in a cycle (bear flattening); the 2-year has risen 133 bp in a year against 112 bp for the 10-year. The other side: the term premium has risen 55 bp in a year and could keep steepening the long end; this is the least confident call.

statement: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate stays between 2.05% and 2.65% on every observation from 2026-10-24 to 2026-12-31.
basis: Breakevens have not moved in a year (+2 bp) through a hiking cycle with PCE inflation at 3.7%, and the annual highs of 2023-2026 are all near 2.5%; the Fed's September language and action are what anchors them. A miss means either a credibility break (above) or a growth scare (below).

statement: The 63-day stock-bond correlation proxy (S&P 500 returns against the fall in the 10-year yield) is positive on 2026-12-31: bonds are still not hedging equities.
basis: The proxy has been positive on 61% of days since 2022 against 8% in 2016-2021, and reads +0.41 now with inflation above target and the Fed hiking: the inflation-driven regime. It flips negative within weeks on a growth scare (it did in late 2023 and early 2025), which is the downside case and the reason the confidence is not higher.
